terms.definition: The brain of the computer that executes program instructions
terms.example: Like a chef in a kitchen processing recipes - reads instructions and performs operations

terms.definition: Temporary memory that holds programs and data while the computer is running
terms.example: Like a desk where you keep papers you're currently working on - fast access but not permanent

terms.definition: Permanent storage for programs, files, and data that persists when computer is off
terms.example: Like a filing cabinet where you store documents long-term

terms.definition: A specific set of instructions written in a programming language for a single task
terms.example: A Python script that prints Hello World - one specific recipe with steps

terms.definition: Collection of one or more programs packaged together to solve larger problems
terms.example: MySQL database system - multiple programs working together

terms.definition: User-facing software with interface designed for end users to accomplish specific tasks
terms.example: WhatsApp mobile app - what you actually use daily

terms.definition: Structured framework defining phases in developing software from concept to maintenance
terms.example: Like building a house - plan, design, construct, inspect, occupy, maintain

terms.definition: Sequential SDLC approach where each phase completes before next begins
terms.example: Like an assembly line - each step fully finishes before moving forward

terms.definition: Iterative SDLC with short development cycles called sprints allowing rapid adaptation
terms.example: Like cooking with constant taste-testing and adjusting recipes

terms.definition: Short development cycle in Agile, typically 1-4 weeks, producing working software
terms.example: Two-week focused work period delivering a new feature

terms.definition: Device or software that initiates requests for resources from a server
terms.example: Your phone (device) running Chrome browser (software) requesting a webpage

terms.definition: Powerful computer or software that processes requests and provides services
terms.example: Amazon's computers serving product pages when you shop online

terms.definition: Model where clients request services and servers provide them via network
terms.example: Restaurant model - customer orders, waiter delivers, kitchen prepares

terms.definition: Application design separating presentation, application logic, and data into three layers
terms.example: Cake with three layers - frosting (UI), cake (logic), plate (data)

terms.definition: Unique numerical identifier for devices on a network
terms.example: Like a house address - 192.168.1.100 identifies your specific computer

terms.definition: Globally unique IP accessible from internet
terms.example: Your website's address that anyone worldwide can reach

terms.definition: IP used within local networks, not routable on internet (10.x, 172.16.x, 192.168.x)
terms.example: Your laptop's address on home Wi-Fi - only works inside your house

terms.definition: Virtual endpoint on server allowing multiple services on one IP address
terms.example: Apartment numbers in a building - IP is building address, port is apartment number

terms.definition: Standardized rules defining how devices communicate over networks
terms.example: Like language rules - English grammar that lets people understand each other

terms.definition: Application protocol for web communication, unencrypted
terms.example: Requesting web pages in plain text - anyone can read the conversation

terms.definition: HTTP with SSL/TLS encryption for secure web communication
terms.example: Encrypted conversation - like speaking in secret code

terms.definition: Connection-oriented protocol guaranteeing reliable, ordered data delivery
terms.example: Certified mail with signature - ensures package arrives intact

terms.definition: Connectionless protocol sending data quickly without delivery guarantees
terms.example: Regular mail - faster but might get lost, fine for video streaming

terms.definition: Protocol for secure remote access to servers, uses port 22
terms.example: Secure phone call to your server to give it commands

terms.definition: Protocol for GUI access to Windows servers, uses port 3389
terms.example: Remote controlling a Windows computer like you're sitting in front of it

terms.definition: Large upfront investments in physical assets providing value over years
terms.example: Buying a car for $30,000 upfront - you own it but pay everything now

terms.definition: Ongoing recurring costs for services consumed, pay-as-you-go
terms.example: Using Uber - pay per ride only when you use it

terms.definition: Delivery of computing resources over internet on pay-per-use basis
terms.example: Electricity from power grid - plug in and pay for what you use

terms.definition: Company delivering computing resources over internet (AWS, Azure, GCP)
terms.example: Electric company providing power - you don't build your own plant

terms.definition: Largest cloud provider with 32% market share, launched 2006
terms.example: The Amazon of cloud computing - started first, biggest selection

terms.definition: Cloud characteristic allowing instant resource provisioning without human interaction
terms.example: ATM machine - get cash anytime without bank teller

terms.definition: Cloud resources can scale up or down automatically based on demand
terms.example: Rubber band - stretches when needed, shrinks when not

terms.definition: Provider shares infrastructure across customers using multi-tenant model
terms.example: Apartment building - shared foundation, walls, but separate units

terms.definition: Cloud systems meter usage and bill based on consumption
terms.example: Taxi meter - pay based on exactly how far you traveled

terms.definition: Cloud provides virtual infrastructure, customer manages OS and applications
terms.example: Renting apartment - building provided, you furnish and maintain interior

terms.definition: Cloud manages infrastructure and platform, customer focuses on applications
terms.example: Furnished apartment - everything provided, you just move in

terms.definition: Complete applications delivered over internet, fully managed by provider
terms.example: Hotel stay - everything managed, you just use the service

terms.definition: Infrastructure shared across multiple organizations over internet
terms.example: Public transportation - shared bus, pay per ride, anyone can use

terms.definition: Dedicated infrastructure for single organization
terms.example: Private car - exclusive use, you control everything

terms.definition: Combination of public and private clouds with orchestration between them
terms.example: Own car plus Uber - use both depending on situation

terms.definition: AWS service providing virtual servers (IaaS)
terms.example: Renting virtual computers in the cloud - you install OS and software

terms.definition: AWS object storage service for files and data
terms.example: Unlimited digital storage box in the cloud

terms.definition: Automatic adjustment of compute capacity based on demand
terms.example: Restaurant automatically adding tables during busy hours, removing when quiet

terms.definition: AWS free resources for learning and experimentation, 12 months for new accounts
terms.example: Free trial period - try services before committing to paid usage
